decision.regression_risk:
The risk is moderate, and it is the same trade-off the earlier ordering levers hit (binding_first, heading_relevance and trigram 0.35 were all net zero). Inside a fixed 1,200-char reserve, every new section admitted can cost another section its second row.

- Who is exposed: any plain question (no named provision, docket or guidance) whose reserve walk has two rows of one section ahead of another section's first row. In P2_on_352, 147 of the 194 questions where the reserve applied reserved 2 or more rows. In C2_on_cosmetics, 27 of 100 have a same-section eCFR pair in context plus a different-section eCFR row dropped for budget. That 27 is an upper bound and includes 2298, 2646 and 2725.
- The harmful case: the key section ranks first in RC1, its required paragraph is its second row, and that row is discovery tier. Discovery rows get nothing from the soft budget once guidance is present, so the displaced paragraph is lost and an unrelated section's row takes its slot. Candidates for this include COS-740.12-Q1, COS-720.4-Q3, COS-82.6-Q1 and COS-70.19-Q2. Rough corpus lengths suggest 82.6-Q1 and 70.19-Q2 do not change. 740.12 and 720.4 are not in the corpus snapshot, so they remain unresolved.
- Heading-promoted (supporting) second rows are at lower risk: they re-enter at the front of the soft-budget walk, as 73.50(c) does in 2725.
- Possible upside, unverified: COS-701.3-Q1, where the key 701.3(b) was dropped while two 801.430 rows were reserved.
- No effect expected on questions that name a provision or docket, guidance questions, or negative controls, because _binding_reserve_applies is false for them.
- With the switch off, behaviour must be byte-identical.

2. no_change.
